about.title: Mammoth Lakes Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Mammoth Lakes is a small town of just under 8,000 people, and a sudden death here is rarely anonymous. Neighbors notice. Coworkers at the resort, along Main Street, or up Minaret Road feel it. Public records for 2025 show zero traffic deaths within town limits, which speaks well of the community, yet losses still happen in other ways: a fall on a poorly maintained property, an accident on a job site, a collision on Route 203 or Old Mammoth Road involving a visitor unfamiliar with mountain conditions, or a medical error that should have been caught. California law gives certain surviving family members the right to bring a civil wrongful death action against the party responsible. That claim is separate from any criminal case and does not depend on one being filed. Through it, a family can seek funeral and burial costs, the financial support the person would have provided, and the harder-to-measure loss of love, companionship, and guidance. LawProactive simply puts you in touch with an independent attorney who can review what happened. There is no charge for the connection, and the attorney works on contingency.

whyChoose.title: Why Families in Mammoth Lakes Reach Out Through LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing, with a spouse or domestic partner and children first in line, followed by certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can explain where your family fits before anyone spends time on paperwork.

items.title: The Two-Year Clock Is Real
items.desc: Most wrongful death actions in California must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is shorter when a government entity is involved. Getting connected early keeps those options open.

items.title: No Fee Unless There Is a Recovery
items.desc: Our service is free, and the attorneys in our network work on contingency. Your family can have the case reviewed without adding a bill to an already heavy month.

items.question: The person who caused the death was a visitor, not a Mammoth Lakes resident. Does that change anything?
items.answer: Not in terms of your right to bring a claim. Mammoth Lakes sees a steady flow of out-of-town drivers on Route 203 and Main Street, and a wrongful death action can be pursued in California regardless of where the responsible party lives. An attorney will look at insurance coverage and jurisdiction so your family doesn't have to sort that out alone.

items.question: Do we have to wait for a criminal case to finish before filing?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil matter and runs on its own track, whether or not prosecutors ever bring charges. Waiting can actually work against you because the two-year filing deadline keeps running. Many families move forward on the civil side while any criminal process unfolds separately.

items.question: What losses can our family actually recover?
items.answer: California allows recovery of funeral and burial expenses, the financial support your loved one would reasonably have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. Every family's situation is different, and no attorney can promise a particular result. What they can do is explain how those categories apply to your circumstances and what evidence supports them.
